# Gospel of Thomas, Saying 99 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Source:** Nag Hammadi Codex II, p. 51 | Coptic

---

## Saying 99

The disciples said to him: "Your brothers and your mother are standing outside." He said to them: "Those here who do the will of my Father — these are my brothers and my mother. They are the ones who will enter the kingdom of my Father."

---

**Council Notes:**

- Thomas's family-of-God saying (cf. Mark 3:31-35 par.) adds the eschatological promise: "will enter the kingdom of my Father." This is Thomas's distinctive contribution.
- "Those here who do the will of my Father": the criterion is both presence (here, inside) and action (doing the will). The biological family is "outside" — both physically and spiritually.
- "Standing outside" (EMET/LOGOS): the Coptic *aheratou ebol* = standing outside. PNEUMA's "waiting outside" adds an expectation that is not in the text.
- "My Father" is used twice — marking both the criterion (will of my Father) and the destination (kingdom of my Father). The familial language is sustained.
